newsitem.title: USA: General Housewares sees Q3 near break-even.
newsitem.headline: General Housewares sees Q3 near break-even.

text.p: General Housewares Corp said it expects third-quarter results to be slightly above break-even, compared to net income of $605,000, or $0.16 per share, in the year-ago period.

The company said delays in reengineering of its warehouse operations in September resulted in shipment delays of two to four weeks. At month's end, there were more than $3.5 million of unshipped September orders as a result. Total backlog at the end of September was $11.5 million versus $6.5 million at the end of September 1995, the company said.

In the third quarter, the company said it completed a restructuring, including the sale of its Sidney Division, the closing of an underperforming retail store and the disposition of certain non-core product lines and inventory.
"These restructuring activities accounted for approximately $600,000 in operating losses for the quarter," said chief financial officer Robert Gray.

"We are obviously disappointed with our inability to ship a substantial portion of our late August and September orders in a timely fashion. However, the comprehensive overhaul of our distribution capability was necessary to achieve desired efficiencies...With most of the problems of the implementation now identified, the substantial order backlog is being reduced and will be shipped during the fourth quarter."

General Housewares makes cutlery, kitchen tools, specialty cookware items, wood products and precision tools for the housewares and craft/hardware markets. It also operates the Chicago Cutlery Etc. retail store chain.
